title: Sticky Date and Brown Butter Porridge
changes_from_base: Dates are softened in browned butter and mashed to a sticky paste before the oats and milk go in, so the porridge is sweetened by the dates rather than maple syrup; fresh pear, flaky salt and cream go on top.
summary: Soft dates and nutty brown butter create instant sweetness in this two-bowl porridge, crowned with fresh fruit and optional cream.

ingredients.item: Medjool dates, stoned and torn into pieces
ripe pear, chopped (or other fresh fruit)

steps.title: Brown butter and dates
steps.text: Melt 14 g butter in a small saucepan over medium heat and cook, stirring, about 2 min until it foams and browns, then add 4 Medjool dates (torn into pieces) and 120 ml water; cook undisturbed 1-2 min until soft, then mash into a paste.

steps.title: Grains and milk
steps.text: Stir in 300 ml milk, 70 g rolled oats, ¼ tsp vanilla and ⅛ tsp cinnamon.

steps.title: Simmer
steps.text: Bring to a simmer and cook 4-6 min, stirring now and then, until tender and as thick as you like.

steps.title: Finish
steps.text: Sprinkle with ⅛ tsp flaky salt, add chopped fresh pear (or other fruit) and a drizzle of cream if using.

tips: Mash the dates thoroughly so they dissolve into the cooking liquid and create a natural sauce.
Brown butter adds deep flavour; listen for the bubbling to quiet slightly, signalling it's ready.
Serve with pear, fresh apple or berries—whatever fruit is in season.
storage: Best served immediately; if you have leftovers, keep them covered in the fridge for 1 day and reheat gently with a splash of milk. Cool leftovers in a shallow container and refrigerate within 2 hours (within 1 hour on a day above 32°C).
